mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.4 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate hiring slowdowns reduce earnings visibility.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases by >0.4pp in a month.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) and accommodative monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 2.0%) indicate stagflation risks, which typically cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real rates rise and growth fears intensify.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0 and FEDFUNDS < 2.0.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions characterized by strong GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.5%) and slowing housing starts (HOUST monthly growth < 0.5%), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in an impending slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the late-cycle expansion regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) reflects robust consumer spending, which typically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in stronger economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS increases for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production below 102.0 (from the 2017=100 base) signals weakening manufacturing activity, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as supply chain disruptions reduce corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 102.0.

mechanism_narrative: Strong job growth (PAYEMS monthly growth > 0.5%) combined with accommodative monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%) signals a robust economy with low interest rates, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings growth accelerates.
regime_hint: strong labor market with loose policy
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS < 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: During supply shock episodes characterized by declining industrial production (INDPRO < 104.0) and slowing GDP growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth < 1.0%), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in reduced corporate profitability from constrained output.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the supply shock regime.
